title: Enterprise revenue routing and cost reconciliation playbook
creator: Leah Patel
description: Create a reproducible intake, prioritization, and routing playbook for non-bug enterprise pricing and billing requests (commitments, invoicing exceptions, marketplace offset allocations, and ad-hoc credit adjustments). This playbook should reduce decision latency, ensure consistent cost allocation to the right finance/cs owners, and provide a clear fast-track path for revenue-impacting requests.
acceptance_criteria: A single canonical intake form hosted in Confluence or Zendesk with required fields and auto-populated customer metadata
A deterministic scoring function that maps requests to one of three lanes: Fast-Track (24-48h SLA), Standard (1-2 sprints), Evaluate (quarterly review)
Routing table linking lanes to owners: Billing Ops, Finance Commitments, Marketplace Reconciliation, Sales Finance
Pre-approved cost-allocation templates for common request types (commitment split, marketplace offset, invoicing exception) documented and accessible
Dashboard widget in Console/Notion showing backlog by lane, age, and expected revenue impact
Documented escalation path with roles, SLAs, and required audit log attachments for any invoice/credit adjustments
triage_rubric: Weighted score built from inputs: Revenue Impact (ARR change), Contract Status (signed/negotiating), Legal/Regulatory Constraint, Implementation Effort (est points), Strategic Signal (marketplace/partner), and Urgency (time to close). Each input has clear enumerated values in the intake form. Scores >= 17 => Fast-Track; 9-16 => Standard; <=8 => Evaluate/Backlog.
scoring_matrix: Contract Status: 0 (no contract), 2 (negotiating), 4 (signed but not committed), 6 (signed with commitment)
Urgency: 0 (no deadline), 2 (customer requested timeline), 4 (SRE/business outage risk)
routing_rules: Requests are first validated by CS intake. Attach signed contract extract when available. Compute score automatically. Fast-Track => assign to Billing Ops and alert Finance Commitments; Standard => assign to Product PM queue for follow-up and copy Billing Ops; Evaluate => add to monthly pricing review board with CS and Sales Finance representation.
cost_allocation_templates: Commitment split: percentage allocation across product lines and marketplace credits; template includes GL codes and required approvals
Invoicing exception: standard credit memo flow with fields for original invoice, reason code, tax implications, and required CFO sign-off threshold
Marketplace offset: alignment mapping between marketplace credit pool and customer-led discounts; three-tier templates for <5k, 5k-50k, >50k offsets
escalation_path: Triage Owner (Billing Ops) - initial decision and <48h action
Finance Commitments - review for revenue recognition and contract treatment
Legal - required when regulatory or contract modifications necessary
VP Revenue Operations - for any adjustments >$250k or with cross-region implications
stakeholders: Finance Commitments - approval for ARR-affecting changes
Sales Finance/Account Exec - provide customer context
Customer Success - intake and customer communications
Platform Reliability/SRE - only if changes require invoice-affecting rollout
dependencies: PM-74215 (Billing Ops automation for credit memos)
PM-81211 (Console dashboard widget for billing backlog)
notes: Design decision: prefer deterministic rules over ad-hoc PM judgment to scale across volume
Trade-off: strict thresholds may surface false positives; mitigation: weekly calibration by finance and CS
Open question: should we support retroactive marketplace credits beyond 90 days? Recommend legal/finance input before policy change
